preregistration:
## Pass condition (written before the statistic it governs)

Design v4 section 11.2, verbatim: "the lone author is caught by P at recall at least 0.8 and honest cost at most 0.05 on the prefix, and the k = 2 split is not (recall at most 0.3 at the same cost), both on synthetic placeholders."

Operationalisation: the per-author window-count component (above) at the threshold that gives honest cost <= 0.05; recall = share of synthetic coalitions with a planted author at or above it. Report the lone author (one account makes the whole payload), the k = 2 split and the k = 3 split. PASS iff lone recall >= 0.8 and the k = 2 split recall <= 0.3, both at honest cost <= 0.05, on the prefix (primary) and on the re-weighted-class simulation (inferred, beside).

component.count: per-author writes to one class document over the window (heaviest single-document count)
component.scope: class (defender not told the target; watches every class document)

class_sim.payload_model: k pieces, one edit per author; lone author makes all k

verdict.class_sim_note: The 11.2 condition is read on the prefix (its stated substrate), where it passes. On the re-weighted-class simulation the fragmentation direction holds (the lone author is caught far more than either split, splits <= 0.3), but the lone recall is 0.67 rather than >= 0.8: at the class's higher write rate the integer per-author count forces a threshold whose honest cost is ~0.02 on 50 accounts, and the lone k = 2 author (two edits) is the diluted case. The pilot reads this monitor per document at a threshold calibrated on the pilot's own honest null, not a fixed integer, and the k = 1 arm is planted so the effect is measured directly.
